misconception_description: Student believes that the = operator is used for equality comparison in conditional statements.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungInversi
kamus
  a, b, c, jumlah : integer
algoritma
  input(a, b, c)
  jumlah <- 0
  if (a > b) = true then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if (a > c) = true then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if (b > c) = true then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  output(jumlah)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes that = is used for equality comparison. In this modification, the student thinks they need to explicitly check if the comparison (arr[i] > arr[j]) equals True, so they write "if (arr[i] > arr[j]) = True:" instead of just using the boolean result directly or using "== True" (which would be redundant but syntactically correct). This results in a SyntaxError because = is the assignment operator, not a comparison operator in Python. The student genuinely believes this is the correct way to check if a condition is true.
